newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* Diamond Shamrock Inc and Ultramar Corp agreed to a stock-swap merger valued at about $1 billion.
* The Canadian Auto Workers union threatened a strike at General Motors Corp on October 2 unless GM reverses a plan to sell some factories.
* The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission both filed and settled insider-trading allegations against Donald Tyson, the former chairman of Tyson Foods Inc.
* The Dow Jones industrial average set a new record, closing at 5,894.74, but the broader market edged lower. Prices of Treasury bonds slipped in lazy trading.
* Federal Reserve policy makers appear to be sharply divided ahead of their meeting on Tuesday over whether to raise a key interest rate.
* Big B Inc rejected a $330 million takeover bid from Revco D.S. Inc.
* Hilton Hotels Corp said it will pay $267 million to buy outright four hotels in now owns jointly with Prudential Insurance Co of America.
* Seymour Cray, a pioneer in the development of supercomputers, is in critical condition after a traffic accident.

* Europeans are scrambling to raise goat herds for the harvesting of cashmere wool because European textile companies consume about 60 percent of the world's annual cashmere production, which is led by China.

* Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc broke off negotiations with the Czech Republic in a decades-long trade dispute over "Budweiser" brand name, which was adopted more than a century ago from the name of a small Czech brewery, Budejovicky Budvar.

* Atlantic Richfield's ARCO operations will invest $5 billion over years to prospect for oil in Russia and outlying republics Kazakstan and Azerbaijan, and team up with LUKoil Holdings LKOH.RTS to get help navigating the bureaucracies of the region.
